resolution.rationale: Upstream v0.91.0 does not touch goal negotiation: goals stay AIR-only upstream and there is no provider-neutral opt-in. #1352 adds sessionWorktrees to the two sessionIndex sentences of docs/air-extensions.md, the same lines where the patch documents top-level _meta.goal for an opted-in non-AIR client, so replaying the v0.89 adaptation conflicts only there. The replacement keeps upstream's sessionWorktrees wording and re-adds the goal sentence; its src/acp-agent.ts, src/goal-extension.ts and test lines are identical to the v0.89 adaptation, and the goal tests pass on v0.91.0.
tests: npm run test:run -- src/tests/acp-agent.test.ts -t "advertises and publishes goals for an opted-in non-AIR client|publishes active_goal as provider-neutral session state without changing turn settlement|advertises async tasks with steering and goals for an opted-in non-AIR client"

resolution.rationale: Upstream async tasks remain AIR-only in v0.91.0. #1352 rewrites the docs/air-extensions.md sessionIndex sentences where the patch documents the top-level _meta["async-tasks"] advertisement, so the v0.90 adaptation conflicts only there; the replacement keeps upstream's sessionWorktrees wording and the patch's documentation. #1348 declares perTaskStopAffordance for subagents-RFD clients and sets stopsWorkflowsOnCancel = perTaskStopAffordance && !clientSupportsAsyncTasks(...). With this patch clientSupportsAsyncTasks is true for a non-AIR client that opted in with _meta["async-tasks"]: true; that client receives each local_workflow as an async task and can stop it with _session/async_task/stop exactly like AIR with asyncTasks, so leaving its workflows running after a parent cancel is the intended composition. A new create-session-options test covers that client; it fails when clientSupportsAsyncTasks is made AIR-only again.
tests: npm run test:run -- src/tests/async-tasks.test.ts src/tests/acp-agent.test.ts src/tests/create-session-options.test.ts src/tests/tool-call-contract.test.ts src/tests/native-subagents.test.ts
npm run test:run -- src/tests/create-session-options.test.ts -t "per-task stop affordance"

resolution.rationale: Upstream v0.91.0 still lists advisor_tool_result among the ignored content blocks of toAcpNotifications, so the patch is not absorbed. The v0.91.0 changes to src/acp-agent.ts that close tool calls a cancel or an abandoned cycle left open (#1334, #1335, #1336, #1339, #1342, #1344) do not touch the advisor path; the patch still resolves the advisor server tool through the normal tool_result path, so its tool call is completed instead of being closed as abandoned. The v0.90 adaptation 590b7ed9e90414124c60eb0b853ad6ed4575a24c replays cleanly and unchanged on v0.91.0, and the incomplete-tool suite, including the new upstream tests, passes with it.

Upstream v0.91.0 has no _alas/context_usage request or contextUsage advertisement, and Claude Agent SDK 0.3.300 (#1355) keeps Query.getContextUsage({ detail }) and SDKControlGetContextUsageResponse. The patch is written on top of the provider-neutral async task adaptation, which is adapted again for v0.91.0, and the sync replays original downstream commits before adaptation commits, so the v0.90 commit conflicts in src/acp-agent.ts and its test. The replacement reapplies the unchanged source and test on top of the v0.91 async task adaptation, and adds a test for #1353: session/resume with changed settings now recreates a live session's query through recreateLiveSession, and the request must read the recreated query rather than the closed one. The new test also gives the replacement a stable patch-id distinct from the retired 1f6defde36ba0a5da34259b72bd74dde30e45f42, so the next sync cannot skip its replayed copy as retired. Both context usage tests fail without the source change.
tests: npm run test:run -- src/tests/acp-agent.test.ts -t "advertises and serves the context usage breakdown"
npm run test:run -- src/tests/create-session-options.test.ts -t "serves the context usage of the query that a resume recreated"
